property_summary: After calling Collect with any arguments, the MinSum value is unchanged from before the call.
After calling Collect with any arguments, setting MinSum after initialization via SetMinSum reverts.
MinSum must not change after initialization is complete.
A successful Collect() call does not change the MinSum state variable.
After Initialized() is called, calling SetMinSum does not change the MinSum value.
The value of MinSum is always equal to the parameter passed to SetMinSum after initialization.
After Collect reverts, the state variable MinSum is either 0 or unchanged from its last SetMinSum call.

After any sequence of calls ending with a call to Collect(uint256), MinSum must be equal to the last parameter passed to SetMinSum (which, due to initialization, is stored only if SetMinSum was called before Initialized); otherwise MinSum must be 0.
After a call to Collect(uint256), if it doesn't revert, the MinSum state variable remains unchanged from its current value.

After any call to Collect, MinSum equals the last value passed to SetMinSum (which is only stored before initialization), and since SetMinSum is only callable before initialization, after initialization MinSum remains unchanged from its final set value.
After a Collect call with any amount, the contract's address balance should equal its previous balance minus the withdrawn amount, unless the call reverts.
After any call to Collect, the contract's address balance is unchanged from before the call, because the reference C always reverts inside Collect due to require(false) in nonReentrant_.
After a Collect call, the contract's LogFile address is never changed if the Collect call reverts (i.e., the contract's state is preserved on revert).
After a call to Collect, the SetLogFile address remains unchanged (equal to the initial zero address) because no external call modifies it.
After any call to Collect, the SetLogFile address remains the same as before the call.
After any Collect call, the Log contract's History always has the same length as the sum of all Put calls' values that were added to the log.
After any Collect call, the state variable `SetLogFile` always retains its initial value (the zero address) because the buggy version never updates it.
After any Collect call, the Log state variable remains address(0) because SetLogFile never updates it.
If SetLogFile is called before initialization, the Log address in C becomes the caller-supplied address; otherwise it remains address(0).
When Log is correctly set, Collect emits a log entry; when Log is never set, Collect does not emit a log entry.
After any call to Collect, the state variable intitalized remains unchanged (always false before it is set to true).
After any call to Collect, the state variable 'intitalized' equals false (since C.Initialized() never changes it from false, and Collect does not modify it).
After calling Collect, the value of 'intitalized' (accessible via the public getter) is always false if it was false before the call.
After any call to Collect, the public getter 'intitalized' remains false (since Initialized() never sets it to true in the mutated version, and Collect does not modify it).
After any call to Collect, the public getter `intitalized` returns `true` if the call was made after `Initialized()` was called.

After any sequence of Put and Collect calls, the Collect function should only succeed when the sender's balance is at least MinSum and the required amount and the current time exceeds the unlock time.
For the reference C, after a Collect call with amount 0, the sender's balance never increases; for the mutant M, it can decrease incorrectly.
The Collect function should only succeed when the sender's balance is at least MinSum and the required amount and the current time exceeds the unlock time.
After a call to Collect with a given amount, the sum of all account balances (tracked by Acc) never exceeds the previous sum plus the msg.value of any preceding Put calls.
After a Collect call, if it reverts then the sender's Acc balance remains unchanged; otherwise the sender's balance decreases by exactly the withdrawn amount.
After a Collect call, the balance recorded in the holder's struct should be less than or equal to the prior balance plus any sent value in the same transaction.
After a Collect call that succeeds (does not revert), the balance of the caller in the contract should be less than or equal to the previous balance plus the amount sent in that transaction.
After any Collect call, the msg.sender's balance in the contract should reflect the sent value if the call was preceded by a Put.
After a Collect call that succeeds (does not revert), the msg.sender's balance in the contract is unchanged (no increase) even if msg.value is sent along with the call.
After a Collect call, the sum of all balances in the contract (i.e., the contract's ether balance) is at least the sum of the balances recorded in the Acc mappings for all participants.
For any caller and amount, if collect succeeds (does not revert) then the caller's balance must strictly decrease by the exact withdrawn amount.

After Collect is called, if the transaction does not revert, the caller's balance in the contract must strictly decrease by exactly the withdrawn amount, and the condition block.timestamp > acc.unlockTime is required for withdrawal; with >= the rule fails when block.timestamp equals acc.unlockTime.

After Collect is called, if the function does not revert and the caller had at least MinSum balance and block.timestamp >= acc.unlockTime but block.timestamp != acc.unlockTime, then the caller's balance in the contract must have decreased by at least the amount requested; for reference, when block.timestamp == acc.unlockTime, Collect must revert.
After Collect is called, if the transaction does not revert and block.timestamp == acc.unlockTime, then the caller's balance must not change (withdrawal is blocked in the reference).

After Collect is called, if the transaction does not revert and block.timestamp == acc.unlockTime, then the caller's contract balance must increase (due to the Put triggered by the external call) rather than decrease (reference reverts at equality, mutant allows withdrawal).
A user can only collect if their balance is strictly greater than MinSum in the buggy version, but in the reference version, balance equal to MinSum is allowed.
After any sequence of actions ending with Collect, the contract's balance decreases exactly by the amount collected if the call succeeds, and reverts otherwise.
When a user's balance equals MinSum, they can always successfully collect that exact amount (if other conditions hold) in the reference, but cannot in the mutant.

When a user's balance exactly equals MinSum and the other conditions hold (balance >= _am and timestamp > unlockTime), the reference allows collecting exactly _am, while the buggy version reverts because it requires balance > MinSum.
A user with balance equal to MinSum can still collect (positive amount) when the other conditions hold, i.e., Collect does not revert for such a user.

When Collect is called with _am equal to the current balance, the balance should be decreased by exactly _am if the preconditions are met (balance >= MinSum and timestamp > unlockTime), but the buggy version prevents the transfer when acc.balance == _am.
If the caller's balance equals _am and the preconditions are met, Collect should succeed in the original but the bug requires balance > _am.
After Collect(_am) reverts, the caller's balance remains unchanged.
If MinSum is 0, the sender's balance equals _am, and block.timestamp exceeds unlockTime, then Collect(_am) must succeed (not revert) and decrease the sender's balance by _am.

When Collect is called with _am equal to the sender's balance and all other preconditions hold, the original contract transfers the full amount and updates the balance, while the buggy version does not send the ether and leaves the balance unchanged.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect(uint256), the balance of the caller is never decreased by more than the value sent to that caller.
The balance of the caller is only decreased when the external call in Collect() succeeds.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, if Collect reverts then the caller's balance in Acc remains unchanged.
After a call to Collect(uint256) that does not revert, the caller's Acc.balance is decreased only when the external call to msg.sender succeeds.
After Collect(uint256), the caller's Acc.balance should be decreased by _am only if the external call succeeds, i.e., when _s is true.
